questions.stem: A student says: 'A catalyst works by giving particles more energy so they can react.' Is this correct?

options.text: Yes, catalysts transfer energy to the reacting particles
No, catalysts lower the activation energy by providing an alternative pathway, so more particles already have enough energy
Yes, catalysts increase the temperature of the reaction
No, catalysts increase the collision frequency instead

questions.explanation: Catalysts do not give particles more energy or increase temperature. Instead, they provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy. This means a greater proportion of the existing collisions already have enough energy to react, increasing the rate.
